description:
From: GC. Approved by the user 2026-11-24 (verbatim "ignore it then; proceed.", answering the fz-9x7.47 obsolescence audit).

Evidence (audit of #880 at 4b56bb8e8): block_pool.rs keeps per-thread free lists (block_pool.rs:351-399) plus a process-wide spill list that #880 added (spill_all, the try_with fallback). The runtime spawns no threads (no thread spawn in src, crates or runtime besides clock.rs sleep); only cargo test threads have separate pools. block_pool_test.rs:121/296/331 spawn threads only to exercise the spill; gift_test's pool_total_cached_blocks and pool_drain_for_test pin per-thread pooling. guides/memory.html:1162 says "any worker".

Decide: keep per-thread pools + spill with the reason written down (Rust thread-safety without a lock in production), or one process-wide pool under the single-worker invariant, at whatever synchronisation cost the bench shows. Either way the thread tests and pool_drain_for_test are restated to the chosen shape.

Done when: one pool shape with its reason in block_pool.rs's module doc; no structure exists only for test threads unless the doc says why; bench guards hold.
title: The block pool's shape is decided for one worker
